name: Ritz-Carlton Residences (Hotel Bossert)
eyebrow: Brooklyn Heights Historic District · Landmarks review
intro: The 1909 Hotel Bossert, a 14-story landmark-district hotel the Jehovah's Witnesses used as guest housing for decades [[sixsqft,wiki]], is being converted into about 61 luxury condos branded as The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Brooklyn Heights, with a 15th-floor rooftop addition [[pineapple,sixsqft]].

status.headline: Landmarks signed off; building permits are next
paragraphs: The Landmarks Preservation Commission approved the revised plan 9–0 on Sept 1, 2026, after hearing the first version on June 23 and sending it back [[pineapple]]. The approval covers a 15th-floor rooftop addition set back from the street, changes to the 13th-floor cornice, and mechanical equipment moved down to the 12th-floor roof [[pineapple,sixsqft]].

The developer filed the conversion with the Buildings Department on Oct 22, 2026 (job B01443511: "convert existing 14-story hotel to residences and add a 1-story addition", with an amended certificate of occupancy) [[dobconv]]. It's in plan review [[dobconv]]. Scaffolding, a sidewalk shed and facade restoration permits are already issued [[dobscaf,dobshed]].

The condo offering plan was submitted to the Attorney General on July 30, 2026 and is awaiting acceptance [[pineapple]]. No City Planning approval is needed: residential use is allowed under the R6 zoning [[pluto]].

facts: SLCE Architects [[sixsqft]]; preservation consultant Higgins Quasebarth & Partners [[pineapple]]

track.intro: The building is in the Brooklyn Heights Historic District, so exterior work needs Landmarks approval. Everything else is Buildings Department permits and the condo offering plan.

steps.t: Public hearing on the first proposal; no action
Plans approved and work permit issued

calendar.intro: No public hearings are scheduled. Landmarks review is finished.

events.n: Commissioners found the new top floor too dominant.

events.n: Rooftop addition set back; equipment moved to the 12th-floor roof.

watch.p: Montague and Hicks are tight streets with heavy foot traffic. Watch for sidewalk sheds, crane and street-closure permits in Updates.

The approved 15th floor is set back to be less visible from the street [[pineapple]]. The DOB plans should match what LPC approved; any later change to the exterior goes back to LPC staff or a hearing.
Reports say 61 [[pineapple]] or 62 [[sixsqft]] condos. The offering plan, once accepted, will settle it.

footer: Watched records: Buildings Department filings and ACRIS recorded documents for Block 248, Lot 15 [[pluto]]. LPC approvals aren't in a machine-readable feed; the daily review checks LPC's calendar.
